A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same optical encoding and guided patch-diffusion work, despite retitling and substantial expansion. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and included appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation results, including reconstruction comparisons, model and lens ablations, cross-dataset evaluation, and measurement-noise experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulation results and adds physical prototype measurements, tabletop reconstructions, CASSI evaluations, and controlled failure analyses.

M1.justification: The core diffusion, patch rescaling, and guidance algorithm remains. However, v3 adds a substantial physical-system adaptation using calibrated measured PSFs, spatial-offset augmentation, and rank-8 LoRA finetuning. Supplement Section 4.6 also introduces desheared-cube conditioning and CASSI-specific guidance; Section 4.3 adds an optional scheduled-guidance procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained ARAD1K, ICVL, Harvard, and CAVE coverage, v3 adds real tabletop measurements from a fabricated metalens, CASSI reconstruction on KAIST at benchmark and higher resolutions, and synthetic checkerboards with controlled spatial homogeneity. These introduce substantial new physical and input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: The original eight ARAD1K comparison methods remain. v3 adds UNet-Regress, a full-image MSE regression control using its backbone, and introduces MST-S/MST-L comparators in the new CASSI comparison. The CASSI baseline values are explicitly imported from cited work rather than reported as rerun experiments.

E3.justification: New protocols include six-scene finetuning/eight-scene prototype testing, 640×960×26 reconstruction with 10 guidance iterations, and CASSI evaluation with 28-channel outputs and uncertainty-based pixel exclusion. For retained training, reported EMA decay changes from 0.9999 to 0.99; the written PSNR formula also changes. These disclosures do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds experimental PSF shift-invariance checks, a LoRA ablation, controlled checkerboard failure analysis, backbone-regression comparisons, denoising trajectories, and per-wavelength uncertainty analysis. CASSI pixel-rejection results additionally test whether uncertainty identifies reconstruction errors. Existing patch, lens, and noise analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: v3 supplementary Figure 7 introduces 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for per-wavelength uncertainty–error correlations. Conversely, v2 explicitly specifies 10 reconstructions with different noise seeds, whereas v3 describes repeated sampling using an unspecified N. An increase in sampling runs is not established.

E6.justification: Most original ARAD1K scores remain unchanged apart from rounding. New results include UNet-Regress at 29.12 dB, prototype averages of 31.20 dB/0.894 SSIM/0.157 SAM, and CASSI averages of 35.46 dB/0.95 SSIM under their respective settings. ICVL mean SSIM changes from 0.95 to 0.94, and v2's five-scene CAVE average is omitted.

T1.justification: The optical and guidance derivations are substantially retained. Limited mathematical revisions include changing the stated DDIM noise distribution from N(0, sigma_t) to N(0, sigma_t^2 I), and replacing the max(x, xhat) factor in v2's PSNR definition with a unit-peak formulation in v3 supplementary Equation 10.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains reconstruction through local patch diffusion and global optical guidance. v3 explicitly includes experimental validation, narrows the priority claim from the first demonstration to one of the first, and reframes prospective camera benefits as a tradeoff between optical and computational complexity.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limits concerning homogeneous regions, restricted propagation of global context, and suitability for fast capture rather than fast reconstruction. It also explains misregistration tolerance and simulation-to-hardware discrepancies, interprets LoRA's effects, and expands discussion of what chromatic aberration contributes relative to RGB filtering.

D1.justification: v3 supplies fabrication procedures, laser-based PSF characterization, geometric and spectral calibration, and detailed LoRA settings absent from v2. It also discloses gradient checkpointing and high-resolution reconstruction times. Some information is lost: v2's explicit lens-design repository availability statement and several configuration-table details are not retained.

R1.justification: v3 acknowledges concurrent filterless imaging by Liu et al. and diffusion-based uncertainty work by Romero et al., while adding references supporting metamerism, LoRA, and computational techniques. Some earlier citations, including PatchScaler, disappear. The broad research positioning remains, but exclusive priority is qualified.

P1.justification: The paper is extensively rewritten and reorganized: diffusion background and patch training are merged, cross-dataset evaluation moves earlier, optical comparison and interpretability are combined, and the supplement gains a hierarchical structure and contents list. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: The layout changes from two columns to one, with extensive figure merging and table restructuring. v2's combined reconstruction table is split between main-text filterless results and supplementary RGB results. Numerous new prototype, calibration, uncertainty, LoRA, CASSI, and failure-analysis displays substantially expand the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2's hardware-feasibility claim relied on simulation; v3 adds a fabricated system evaluated against reference hyperspectral captures, with calibration and adaptation documented in detail. Controlled failure analyses and explicit applicability limits further strengthen empirical credibility. Reporting gaps remain, including the stated 15-scene total versus six finetuning/eight test scenes and the omitted sampling count, but these do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
